skill.name: explainer-video
skill.description: Plan 30- to 90-second explainers for products, onboarding, or concepts. Draft narration, build a timed storyboard, align captions, and review the video before export.
skill.summary: Turn one idea into a timed explainer script, storyboard, and caption plan.
skill.author: iart-ai

security_audit.summary: Eighteen alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, including a render comment misidentified as system reconnaissance. Five alerts identify execution risks from unverified helper scripts or Remotion commands that can fetch packages. No evidence was found of prompt injection or data exfiltration.

remediation.issue: Remotion examples can fetch and execute an unpinned package when no matching local CLI is available.
remediation.suggestion: Pin Remotion with a committed lockfile and use the reviewed project-local CLI. Separate dependency installation from rendering and require approval before network access.

remediation.issue: The skill directs users to helper scripts that are not present in the audited snapshot.
remediation.suggestion: Include the helpers in the audited skill and resolve their paths from the skill directory. Otherwise, remove the instructions and the claim that they are packaged.

content.value_statement: A short video can be hard to follow when narration, visuals, and captions are planned separately. This skill puts them on one timeline, from the first script draft to export checks.
actual_capabilities: Draft narration for a 30- to 90-second video around one message and one next step.
Estimate scene durations from narration pace and add time for pauses.
Map each scene to narration, a visual, a transition, and required assets.
Plan diagram reveals, animated keywords, and count-up statistics with a consistent visual style.
Create SRT or VTT caption cues aligned with the timing used for scene changes.
Guide frame-by-frame visual checks and MP4 export in a configured Remotion project.
limitations: Timing estimates need to be checked against the final narration recording.
The skill does not bundle voice recordings or production assets.
Video rendering requires an external setup such as Remotion or After Effects. The listed verification helpers are not included.

use_cases.title: Introduce a Product Feature
use_cases.description: Show how one feature solves a customer problem, then end with one clear next step.

use_cases.title: Teach a First-Time Task
use_cases.description: Storyboard a short walkthrough with narration and captions for employees watching without sound.

use_cases.title: Explain a Technical Concept
use_cases.description: Break a process into scenes that reveal one diagram step at a time.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Short Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a 30-second explainer for [audience] about [topic]. Explain one problem and how the solution works, then end with [next step].
prompt_templates.scenario: You have one topic and need a first narration draft.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Timed Storyboard
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn [approved script] into a 60-second storyboard. List each scene's time range, narration, visual, transition, and assets.
prompt_templates.scenario: You have approved narration and need a scene plan.

prompt_templates.title: Align Captions and Scenes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [transcript with timecodes] to draft VTT cues and align scene changes. Flag any cues that need more reading time.
prompt_templates.scenario: You have recorded narration and need captions for muted playback.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Remotion Export
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [composition] with [final narration and settings] using only the approved local renderer. Check the first frame, each scene, and the last frame before exporting MP4.
prompt_templates.scenario: You have a configured Remotion project and need to verify the final video.

output_examples.input: Storyboard a 30-second introduction to reusable team checklists.
output: 0-6 seconds: Show a team rebuilding its launch checklist. Narration: Every launch starts with the same list.
6-13 seconds: Open the saved checklist library. Narration: Save your usual steps in a reusable template.
13-24 seconds: Select the template and assign one task. Narration: Create a project from the template and give each task an owner.
24-30 seconds: Hold on the checklist. Narration: Save your first template before your next launch.

output_examples.input: Suggest captions and visual timing for a filter that shows open tasks.
output: 0.4-2.6 seconds: Select the Status filter. Highlight the filter as the cue appears.
2.8-4.6 seconds: Choose Open. Hold on the menu so viewers can read the selection.
4.8-7.2 seconds: Only open tasks are shown. Let the updated list settle before the next scene.

best_practices: Read the script aloud and time it before building scenes.
Use the same timing reference for captions and scene changes, then compare both with the final narration.
Inspect a frame from each scene with the final settings before encoding the video.
anti_patterns: Turning one explainer into a tour of unrelated features.
Animating scenes before the narration and runtime are confirmed.
Using a new color meaning or transition style in each scene.

faq.question: How long should the video be?
faq.answer: The workflow targets 30 to 90 seconds. Start near 140 words per minute, then adjust for pauses and technical terms.

faq.question: Can I use it for a script without rendering a video?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask for a script, a timed storyboard, or a caption plan without requesting a render.

faq.question: Which caption formats does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers SRT and VTT cues and explains how to burn captions into the video.

faq.question: Does it include narration audio?
faq.answer: No recordings are bundled. Supply recorded narration or use a separate tool to create it.

faq.question: What do I need to export an MP4?
faq.answer: Use a configured renderer such as Remotion with your composition, narration, fonts, and visual assets. Confirm the renderer and its dependencies before running it.

faq.question: Can I deliver a single web scene instead?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow recommends standalone HTML when the deliverable is a single web scene rather than a video.
